output.myth: Mesket's husband took his boat out past the Leeward rocks in the autumn gales, and the sea kept the boat and the man. Mesket did not weep where the children could see. She filled a sack with salt, slung it on her back, and every month walked the cliff path down to the strait and rowed across to the skerry wives, who had cod and no salt to keep it. She came home with silver, or with fish. Hesk, who winds every string and keeps count, notched each crossing into her reel. When Mesket was old, she tied a lamp to the mast of her boat and went out one last time. Orrun, who carries both seas on his back, felt the small weight of her and did not shrug. She went down into the strait with the salt still on her back, and she came up again as a lamp. Her light hangs over the water where her husband went under. Do not ask her to stop.
